nodes.label: Fail-Closed Design
nodes.rationale: Every failure mode should degrade safely toward denial rather than silent permission: a judge/verification error should resolve to UNCERTAIN/ESCALATE (agentic-judge-layer) or be reported as 'unknown' rather than fabricated as pass/fail (agent-readiness-auditor's Tier-B silence handling), so an ambiguous signal is never mistaken for a verified fact.

nodes.label: Thread-Based Engineering
nodes.rationale: Mental framework (IndyDevDan) for human-AI collaboration: the human shows up at the start (prompt) and end (review), the agent does the middle. Improvement comes from running MORE threads (parallelize), LONGER threads (more autonomy), THICKER threads (nested sub-agents), and FEWER checkpoints (trust via automated validation) rather than tighter step-by-step control.

nodes.label: Avellaneda–Stoikov Market Maker
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the market-maker model because its reservation-price/half-spread formulation lets quotes be pulled during volatility shocks, which is what makes the simulated flash crashes actually crash — a deliberate design choice to reproduce a real market failure mode.

nodes.label: Universal-Variable Kepler Propagator
nodes.rationale: Uses the Sundman/Stumpff universal-variable formulation instead of numerical integration so that every orbital state is a closed-form pure function of epoch, letting the UI scrub time exactly with no drift and covering elliptic/parabolic/hyperbolic orbits with one code path (needed for patched conics).

nodes.label: Mechanism Space
nodes.rationale: Most product teams jump from problem straight to features, skipping the mechanism step where most unbuilt opportunity lives; the skill forces explicit enumeration of causal mechanisms (Problem -> Metric -> Mechanism -> Simulation -> Feature -> Product -> Pricing) before any feature spec is written, so teams don't confidently build the wrong thing.

nodes.label: Mechanism Scoring Formula (V×C×D×T)/(R+F+K)
nodes.rationale: Not meant to produce precise numbers — forces explicit reasoning across value, causal plausibility, data availability, testability, regulatory risk, friction and complexity simultaneously, so an easy mechanism like 'build a dashboard' isn't unconsciously ranked above a harder but higher-value one like 'restructure the incentive system'.

nodes.label: Spherical Cow Cloak (Pendry Transformation-Optics Cloak)
nodes.rationale: Off-diagonal permittivity components exceeding ~1.3x the diagonal cause unconditional Yee-grid instability that cannot be fixed by reducing the Courant number; the minimum stable regularization (eps_min >= 0.55) flattens the gradient-index profile the cloak depends on, so full cloaking and FDTD stability are fundamentally in tension in 3D — documented as a genuine numerical-methods limitation, not a bug, with the 2D cylindrical case shown as the case where the physics and numerics do cooperate.

nodes.label: Key Stack Decisions (Stripe Checkout, Supabase, Prisma v6, Tailwind v3)
nodes.rationale: Stripe Checkout (hosted page) chosen over custom payment UI to eliminate PCI scope; Supabase chosen for both Postgres and Auth to avoid a separate auth service; server-side DB-backed cart chosen over localStorage to survive refresh/cross-device/login-merge; Prisma pinned to v6 because v7 dropped the schema.prisma `url` field needed for Supabase's pooled connection; Tailwind downgraded to v3 because v4 is incompatible with Next.js 16's Turbopack bundler (caused a CssSyntaxError at startup).

nodes.rationale: Every specialist agent is forced through OBSERVE, THINK, REFLECT, CRITIQUE, REFINE, ACT, VERIFY before answering, so responses undergo self-critique rather than being emitted in one uncontrolled pass.

nodes.label: 20-Prompt Research Bank
nodes.rationale: Running all 20 prompts cold is wasteful because many overlap ~70%; the pipeline collapses them into an 8-step sequence where each step consumes the previous step's output, with prompt #2 (margin-pool ranking) gating everything downstream and falsification (#17) deliberately run last and cheapest, only against survivors.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Monte Carlo Design
nodes.rationale: An outer loop varies the assumption set itself (e.g. is demand typically high or low) while an inner loop samples many outcomes per assumption set, so the tool reveals not just what might happen but how sensitive the conclusion is to the assumptions — plain Monte Carlo over one fixed assumption set would hide that sensitivity.

nodes.label: moose-simulation (Claude Code skill)
nodes.rationale: A structured 9-step checklist governing the full MOOSE simulation lifecycle (prerequisites, input-file authoring, Docker execution, output validation, matplotlib visualization, README docs) built from lessons across 21 successful quickstart cases, so an agent can run simulations end-to-end without manual intervention.

nodes.label: docker-windows (Claude Code skill)
nodes.rationale: MINGW/Git Bash on Windows silently rewrites Unix-looking paths and mangles Docker flags (e.g. `-w /work` becomes a Windows path, single-letter flags like `-i` can be eaten), causing Docker to run with no output or wrong results and no error; the fix is the environment variable MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 plus a canonical `--entrypoint /bin/bash -c '...'` command pattern.

nodes.label: Open Engine
nodes.rationale: Shared task queue / blackboard system letting Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex hand off work via a human-readable issue tracker. Decision: skip full adoption for a solo developer because shared queue, locking, routing, and receipts only earn their keep under multi-agent or multi-person conditions; distilled into a 3-habit work-mode template instead (work mode not prompt mode, one scoped task then stop, leave a receipt).

nodes.label: Open Stack
nodes.rationale: Framework for diagnosing agent workflow pain, choosing the right primitive, and keeping memory, methods, approvals, and receipts under the user's control.

nodes.label: Hooks-based memory vs tools-based memory
nodes.rationale: Hooks (automatic background before/after processes) outperform tools-based approaches for memory because context is always available without requiring the model to decide to call a search tool.

nodes.label: OpenSpec
nodes.rationale: Lightweight spec layer so humans and AI agree on requirements before code is written; philosophy is fluid not rigid, iterative not waterfall, brownfield-friendly, scalable from personal projects to enterprises.

nodes.label: PACER learning methodology
nodes.rationale: Classifies content into Procedural/Analogous/Conceptual/Evidence/Reference types and applies the matching strategy (practice, critique, understand, connect, memorize-last-resort). Core insight: retrieval without proper encoding first is 'filling a leaky bucket faster' — encoding (understanding) should precede memorization.

nodes.label: gstack-bridge skill
nodes.rationale: ADR 001: a thin prompt-layer bridge skill (not an adapter patch) lets Paperclip and gstack each stay ignorant of the other. It teaches agents to substitute AskUserQuestion with Paperclip approvals and inline skill chains with async subtask delegation.

nodes.label: 9-agent org chart design
nodes.rationale: ADR 002: 9 separate role-scoped agents chosen over one agent with all 26 skills, because role separation gives each agent a focused context window and a clear human-escalation path; a single super-agent would have a bloated context.

nodes.label: claude-haiku-4-5 model choice
nodes.rationale: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 reliably follows multi-step Paperclip protocol at low cost; the earlier claude-3-haiku-20240307 ignored AGENTS.md and fell back to banned tools regardless of prompt explicitness — model capability mattered more than prompt engineering for headless agents.

nodes.label: Cognitive Decoupling Agent
nodes.rationale: The AI is deliberately an adversarial interlocutor, not a therapist or cheerleader, applying Karl Popper's Falsificationism, Stoic Negative Visualization, and cognitive bias detection to stress-test goals rather than validate them.

nodes.label: Curry-Howard correspondence
nodes.rationale: Structural equivalence between logical proofs and well-typed programs is applied to physics: a conservation law is a type/proposition, a valid collision is a well-typed program/proof, and linear types (use-once) enforce conservation of matter (no particle cloned or silently dropped).

nodes.label: damage-control extension
nodes.rationale: Real-time safety auditing that intercepts dangerous bash patterns (rm -rf, git reset --hard, DROP DATABASE) and enforces path-based access controls (zero-access, read-only, no-delete paths) from a YAML rules file — a hedge against the leader (Claude Code) by exposing safety controls Pi doesn't provide out of the box.

nodes.label: Coqui TTS
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the best open-source voice cloning library, but the maintainer company shut down in 2024, leaving a broken/stale dependency tree requiring a --no-deps workaround. Lesson: assess the maintainer's viability, not just the code — a library from a dead company is a liability, not an asset.

nodes.label: dependency-risk-planner skill
nodes.rationale: Encodes the project's central lesson that dependency problems are planning problems, not debugging problems: runs a pre-flight dependency health audit (maintainer viability, Python version ceilings, API stability) before any code is written, because every failure in the avatar pipeline traced back to a knowable planning-phase gap.
